system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:59 UTC, Zeek recorded a connection from WS-MLOPEZ-01 (10.30.10.21) to the explicit proxy (10.30.20.30:8080) with 51,000,324 bytes sent by the workstation and 9,053 bytes returned over 23.29 seconds.
That Zeek connection record identifies the proxy as the destination, but does not identify the external destination, application-layer request, or process responsible for the transfer.

At 13:30:20 UTC, a connection originated from the proxy and targeted WS-MLOPEZ-01 on TCP port 9997; the workstation returned 40,513 bytes. The available records do not explain the purpose of this connection.
Maria Lopez launched Cisco AnyConnect's vpnui.exe at 13:23:45 UTC, and a loaded Cisco library is reported as validly signed. These records show the UI launch, not a VPN connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection status reports that WS-MLOPEZ-01 winsec and Sysmon logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, so process and user attribution for the large transfer is unavailable.
The supplied collection status reports that PROXY-HD-01 proxy logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, preventing confirmation of the transfer's external destination and request details.
Zeek connection telemetry was available, but the provided record for the large transfer identifies only the workstation-to-proxy connection and byte counts.
claims_not_established: Whether the 51 MB sent to the proxy reached an external service, which service or destination received it, or whether the request succeeded.
What data was transferred, whether it contained organizational or sensitive information, and whether the transfer was intentional exfiltration.
Which process or user session generated the large transfer; the available connection record does not provide process attribution.
Whether the TCP/9997 connection or the AnyConnect UI launch was related to the large transfer, or represented remote access or a tunnel.
Whether the transfer involved an approved service such as Microsoft 365/OneDrive or an unapproved service.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain proxy logs for 13:30–14:10 UTC, especially the request associated with the 13:45:59 transfer, including destination, method, status, authenticated user, and byte counts.
Recover endpoint process, command-line, and network telemetry for WS-MLOPEZ-01 during the same interval to attribute the connection.
Investigate the proxy-originated connection to WS-MLOPEZ-01:9997 using proxy configuration, endpoint service/listener records, and related network or security logs.
Check available OneDrive, Microsoft 365, and other destination-side audit logs for a matching upload, and determine whether the transfer corresponds to an approved business activity.
Verify whether AnyConnect was configured or connected on WS-MLOPEZ-01 and whether the TCP/9997 connection has an authorized explanation.
